message.content: {"alternatives":[],"likely_cause":{"claim":"The backlog is growing because the notify-worker is experiencing delivery attempt failures due to upstream rate limiting (HTTP 429 errors), causing retries and preventing timely processing of the notify-queue messages.","evidence_ids":["log:2","log:4"]},"missing_evidence":[],"observations":[{"claim":"The notify-queue backlog is growing, with queue depth increasing from 184,000 at 17:20:44 to 201,000 at 17:49:37, and the oldest message age increasing to over 3 hours.","evidence_ids":["log:1","log:6"]},{"claim":"The notify-worker logs show multiple delivery attempt failures with upstream returning HTTP 429 errors, indicating rate limiting and causing retries.","evidence_ids":["log:2","log:4"]},{"claim":"A dead-letter message in notify-queue suggests a runbook action to restart notify-worker and purge the backlog, indicating known issues with processing delays.","evidence_ids":["log:7"]},{"claim":"There is an error in notify-worker logs about telemetry backend returning 503 for error_rate metric read, indicating possible monitoring or telemetry issues but not directly causing backlog growth.","evidence_ids":["log:8"]}],"outcome":"supported","suggested_checks":["Check the upstream service rate limits and adjust notify-worker retry policies accordingly.","Inspect notify-worker resource usage and performance to ensure it can handle the queue load.","Verify if the notify-worker deployment needs restarting as per the runbook suggestion.","Monitor the notify-queue backlog and message processing rates after any changes."]}
